kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-01.title: Follow the loose ends
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-01.body:
At the gap, two loose line ends come from the tile on one side and two from the tile on the other side. For two closed loops, each loose end of the left loop has to be joined to the other end of the *same* loop, and the same for the right loop. So the new tile must contain two separate arcs, each connecting the two ends of one loop and not crossing over to the other loop.

Only tile (C) has its two lines in exactly these positions; the others join the loops into one big line or leave ends unconnected.

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-02.title: Order of operations
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-02.body:
Numerator: $20 \times 24 = 480$. Denominator: $2\times0 + 2\times4 = 0 + 8 = 8$. So the value is $480 \div 8 = 60$.

**Answer: (D) 60**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-03.title: Knotted or not
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-03.body:
The rope on the right is a closed loop that is not knotted: the figure eight just has one twist, which can be undone. Without cutting we can only move and twist the loop, so we can only form shapes that are also unknotted.

In (A), (C), (D) and (E) one can undo the crossings by sliding loops over each other. Figure (B) is a trefoil knot: its three crossings alternate over–under–over all the way round, and such a knot cannot be untangled without cutting.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-04.title: Each corner becomes three
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-04.body:
A tetrahedron has 4 corners and 3 edges meet at each. Cutting off a corner removes it and creates a small triangle, whose 3 corners lie on those 3 edges. So each old corner is replaced by 3 new ones: $4 \times 3 = 12$.

**Answer: (D) 12**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-05.title: Strip size
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-05.body:
The side of the square is 32 ÷ 4 = 8 cm. Each strip is 8 cm long and 8 ÷ 4 = 2 cm wide, so its perimeter is 2 × (8 + 2) = 20 cm.

**Answer: (B) 20 cm**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-06.title: List the orders
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-06.body:
There are 6 orders of the cards:

1 | 5 | 11 → 1511, 1 | 11 | 5 → 1115, 5 | 1 | 11 → 5111, 5 | 11 | 1 → 5111, 11 | 1 | 5 → 1115, 11 | 5 | 1 → 1151.

Some give the same number, because 1 next to 11 looks like 11 next to 1. The different numbers are 1511, 1115, 5111, 1151: four of them.

**Answer: (B) 4**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-07.title: Mirror the right half
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-07.body:
Folding along the dashed line flips the right half over onto the left half, like a mirror. Everything on the left half stays where it is.

- The small circle at the top right lands at the top of the left half, near the fold.
- The circle on the left stays.
- The small circle cut by the dashed line at the bottom folds onto itself and shows as a half circle on the fold.
- The curved line on the right is mirrored onto the left half as well.

This is picture (C).

**Answer: (C)**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-08.title: Start with the pickiest
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-08.body:
Berta only likes apples, so she gets the apples. Eva likes apples and cherries; the apples are gone, so Eva gets the cherries. (Then Doris gets grapes, and Anna and Conny share strawberries and bananas.)

**Answer: (E) Eva**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-09.title: Only every second child
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-09.body:
Number the children 0 to 49 around the circle, with Frida as 0. The ball goes to 6, 12, 18, …, always to an even number (counting round the circle by 50 keeps the number even, since 50 is even). Every even number is reached before the ball comes back to Frida: 25 children in each round. Frida gets the ball 100 times, so every round is completed.

The 25 children with odd numbers never get the ball.

**Answer: (D) 25**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-10.title: Compare with quarter-rhombi
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-10.body:
The two diagonals cut the rhombus into 4 congruent right triangles, each with legs equal to half of each diagonal.

Each added grey triangle has a vertical leg from the side corner of the rhombus down to the line $AB$ (half the vertical diagonal) and a horizontal leg along $AB$ to $M$ (half the horizontal diagonal). So each added triangle is congruent to one of the 4 quarter triangles.

Adding 2 quarters to 4 quarters increases the area by $\frac24 = 50\%$.

**Answer: (E) 50 %**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-11.title: Share the gap
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-11.body:
Each piece has an angle of 360° ÷ 10 = 36°. The eaten piece leaves a gap of 36°, which is now shared out equally between the 9 gaps between the 9 pieces: 36° ÷ 9 = 4°.

**Answer: (B) 4°**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-12.title: Try the top-left number
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-12.body:
Write the grid as $\begin{array}{cc} a & b \\ c & d \end{array}$ with $ab = 6$, $cd = 8$, $ac = 4$, $bd = 12$.

- $a = 1$: $b = 6$, $c = 4$, $d = 2$. Check $cd = 8$ ✓ and $bd = 12$ ✓. All different.
- $a = 2$: then $c = 2$ as well — not allowed. $a = 3$ or $6$ does not divide 4.

The numbers are 1, 6, 4, 2 with sum 13.

**Answer: (C) 13**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-13.title: Fractions of the money
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-13.body:
9 of 12 packages use $\frac{3}{4}$ of the money, leaving $\frac14$. A quarter of the money buys $\frac14$ of 20 chocolate bars, i.e. 5.

**Answer: (C) 5**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-14.title: Fill the gaps
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-14.body:
Two shapes can form a cuboid only if the cubes sticking out of one fill exactly the notches of the other (and the cube counts add up to a box size).

Turning shape 3 round, its stepped side fits exactly into the steps of shape 2, and together they form a complete box. For the other pairs, either the steps do not match or a cube would stick out.

**Answer: (B) 2 and 3**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-15.title: Each extra trolley
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-15.body:
Going from 4 to 10 trolleys adds 6 trolleys and 168 − 108 = 60 cm, so each extra trolley adds 10 cm. From 4 trolleys back to 1 we remove 3 × 10 = 30 cm: one trolley is 108 − 30 = 78 cm.

**Answer: (C) 78 cm**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-16.title: Count the light faces
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-16.body:
Each of the 6 light cubes has 5 visible faces: 30 light faces in all.

- The outer end face of each arm can only be covered by a cube placed straight beyond that arm: 6 cubes, each covering just 1 light face.
- The other 24 light faces are the side faces of the arms. A dark cube placed in a "corner" between two neighbouring arms touches 2 of them, and no cube can touch more. So at least 24 ÷ 2 = 12 more cubes are needed, and the 12 corner positions (one for each pair of neighbouring arms) do the job.

Minimum: 6 + 12 = 18.

**Answer: (A) 18**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-17.title: Few horizontal lines
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-17.body:
Only one horizontal line in total, so one digit has no horizontal line and the other has exactly one. From the picture: 1 has no horizontal line (2 vertical); 4 and 7 have one horizontal line, with 3 and 2 vertical lines.

We need 5 vertical lines: 1 and 4 give 2 + 3 = 5. ✓ (1 and 7 give only 4.)

Sum: 1 + 4 = 5.

**Answer: (A) 5**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-18.title: Radii from the height
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-18.body:
Let $R$ be the radius of the big semicircle. It touches the top, so the rectangle is $R$ high. The other radii are $R - 5$ and $R - 7$.

The three diameters fill the length 36 cm: $2R + 2(R-5) + 2(R-7) = 36$, so $6R - 24 = 36$ and $R = 10$.

The rectangle is $36 \times 10$, perimeter $2(36 + 10) = 92$ cm.

**Answer: (B) 92**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-19.title: Total must be a multiple of 4
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-19.body:
The three pieces cover 4 + 5 + 4 = 13 cells, so the fourth piece has 3 cells. Their numbers add up to (2+2+1+2) + (2+1+3+1+1) + (2+3+1+2) = 7 + 8 + 8 = 23.

The 4 rows have equal sums, so the total of all 16 numbers is a multiple of 4. The fourth piece must add $23 + x$ to a multiple of 4:

(A) 1+1+3 = 5 → 28 ✓; (B) 3 → 26; (C) 4 → 27; (D) 6 → 29; (E) 7 → 30.

Only (A) works (each row and column then sums to 7).

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-20.title: Split 44 into 7s and 5s
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-20.body:
The child with 44 fish got 7 on some days and 5 on the others: $44 = 7a + 5b$. Trying $a = 0, 1, 2, \dots$: only $a = 2$, $b = 6$ works ($14 + 30$). So 8 days passed, $8 \times 12 = 96$ fish in total, and the other child got $96 - 44 = 52$.

**Answer: (D) 52**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-21.title: Jumps for each direction
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-21.body:
If the path is $d$ metres, it needs $d$ jumps up and $\frac d3$ jumps down: $d + \frac d3 = \frac{4d}{3} = 2024$, so $d = 1518$. The total distance is $2d = 3036$ m.

**Answer: (D) 3036**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-21.title: Groups of 4 jumps
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-21.body:
For every 3 metres of path there are 3 jumps up and 1 jump down: 4 jumps covering 6 metres. 2024 jumps make 506 such groups: $506 \times 6 = 3036$ m.

**Answer: (D) 3036**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-22.title: Go through the possible axes
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-22.body:
A $4\times4$ square can only have the vertical, horizontal or diagonal middle lines as axes. Number rows and columns 1–4 from the top left; the black cells are (1,2) and (2,3).

- **Vertical axis:** mirror images (1,3) and (2,2) must be black: 1 way.
- **Horizontal axis:** (4,2) and (3,3): 1 way.
- **Main diagonal** (top-left to bottom-right): (2,1) and (3,2): 1 way.
- **Other diagonal** (top-right to bottom-left): the mirror sends (1,2) to (3,4), while (2,3) lies on this diagonal and stays. So (3,4) must be black, and the second new cell must lie on the diagonal itself: (1,4), (3,2) or (4,1) — 3 ways.

That gives 1 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 6 patterns, and none of them has a second axis.

**Answer: (E) 6**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-23.title: Follow the dry part
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-23.body:
Take 100 g of fresh mushroom: 80 g water and 20 g dry matter. The dry matter does not change. In dried mushrooms it is 80 % of the mass, so the dried mass is 20 ÷ 0.8 = 25 g. The mass drops from 100 g to 25 g, a decrease of 75 %.

**Answer: (C) 75**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-24.title: Count corners
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-24.body:
In this pattern every corner point is shared by 2 hexagons and 2 triangles. Each hexagon has 6 corners and each triangle 3.

Counting the corner points via hexagons: $6H \div 2 = 3H$. Via triangles: $3T \div 2$. These are equal, so $3H = \frac32 T$, i.e. $T = 2H$.

With about 3000 hexagons she needs about 6000 triangles.

**Answer: (D) 6000**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-25.title: Write the top box
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-25.body:
Let the bottom row be $a, n, b$. The middle row is $an$ and $nb$, and the top is $an \cdot nb = a\,b\,n^2 = 36$.

So $n^2$ divides 36: $n = 1, 2, 3$ or $6$ (with for example $ab = 36, 9, 4, 1$). That is 4 values.

**Answer: (D) 4**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-26.title: Parallel lines on the grid
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-26.body:
Use grid coordinates: the bottom points are (0,0), (2,0), (4,0) and the top points are (1,3) and (3,3).

- $\beta$ is at (2,0) between the lines to (1,3) and (3,3). By symmetry the vertical line through (2,0) halves it, so each half is the angle between the vertical and a line going 1 across and 3 up.
- $\alpha$ is at (0,0) between the line to (3,3) (the 45° diagonal) and the line to (1,3). The line to (1,3) also goes 1 across and 3 up, so it makes the angle $\frac{\beta}{2}$ with the vertical. The diagonal makes 45° with the vertical. Hence $\alpha = 45° - \frac\beta2$.
- By symmetry $\gamma = \alpha$.

So $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 2\left(45° - \frac\beta2\right) + \beta = 90°$, which is not among (A)–(D).

**Answer: (E) another angle**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-27.title: The rest is a multiple of 3
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-27.body:
Altogether there are 4 + 6 + 12 + 13 + 22 + 29 = 86 eggs. After the purchase, chicken eggs = 2 × duck eggs, so the remaining number of eggs is 3 × duck eggs — a multiple of 3.

86 − 4 = 82, 86 − 6 = 80, 86 − 12 = 74, 86 − 13 = 73, 86 − 22 = 64 are not multiples of 3; 86 − 29 = 57 is. So Christoph bought 29 eggs.

Check: 19 duck eggs (6 + 13) and 38 chicken eggs (4 + 12 + 22).

**Answer: (E) 29**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-28.title: Test each pirate
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-28.body:
The readable answers are Tom: silver 9, bronze 11; Al: gold 7, bronze 12; Pit: gold 10, bronze 10; Jim: gold 9, silver 10. Since the total is 30, a truthful pirate fixes all three numbers.

- Tom truthful: gold 10, silver 9, bronze 11. But then Pit's “gold 10” is true. ✗
- Pit truthful: gold 10, silver 10, bronze 10. Then Jim's “silver 10” is true. ✗
- Jim truthful: gold 9, silver 10, bronze 11. Then Tom's “bronze 11” is true. ✗
- Al truthful: gold 7, silver 11, bronze 12. Tom (9, 11), Pit (10, 10) and Jim (9, 10) are wrong on every answer. ✓

**Answer: (B) Al**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-29.title: Measure the road in Benni-minutes
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-29.body:
Let Benni cover 1 unit per minute, so Anne covers 3. Until the first meeting they cover the whole road together: $15 \times (1 + 3) = 60$ units.

Anne reaches B after $60 \div 3 = 20$ minutes and turns round. Now both drive from B towards A, Benni having a head start. At time $t$ Benni is $t$ units from B and Anne $3(t - 20)$ units from B. They meet when $3(t-20) = t$, i.e. $t = 30$ minutes (Benni has not reached A yet).

**Answer: (C) 30 min**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-29.title: Total distance
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-29.body:
From the start until Anne catches Benni the second time, Anne has driven one full road plus the distance $x$ back from B, and Benni has driven $x$. Anne drives 3 times as far: $60 + x = 3x$, so $x = 30$ units, which takes Benni 30 minutes.

**Answer: (C) 30 min**

kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-30.title: Rectangle plus triangle
kangaroo-at-2024-kadett-30.body:
The pentagon is a rectangle $ABCE$ with an isosceles triangle $EDC$ on top; $D$ is above the midpoint of $AB$. Let each strip have width $w$, the rectangle height $h$ and the triangle height $k$.

Each strip is a rectangle $w \times h$ plus the part of the triangle above it. A strip's area equals its width times its height at the middle of the strip (the top is straight there), except for the middle strip, whose top has a peak.

- Light strip (second from the left): its middle is $\frac{1.5}{2.5} = \frac35$ of the way from $E$ to below $D$, so its area is $wh + \frac35 wk = 10$.
- Dark middle strip: each half has width $\frac w2$ and average height $h + \frac{2.25}{2.5}k = h + \frac{9}{10}k$, so its area is $wh + \frac{9}{10}wk = 13$.

Subtracting: $\frac{3}{10}wk = 3$, so $wk = 10$ and $wh = 4$.

Pentagon $= 5w \cdot h + \frac12 \cdot 5w \cdot k = 5\cdot4 + \frac52\cdot10 = 20 + 25 = 45$.

**Answer: (A) 45**
